Post Date: 2016-02-16T09:28:30Z

Title: Union type of string literals
Description: With TypeScript 1.8, this code fails:

```
type SomeString = ('string1' | 'string2') & ('string3' | 'string4');
const x: SomeString = 'string1';
```

With the following error: `Type 'string' is not assignable to type '("string1" | "string2") & ("string3" | "string4")'. Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"string1" | "string2"'. Type 'string' is not assignable to type '"string2"'`.

Is this by design? Should it not be possible to use unions for string literal types?
